content.text: The Library is not divided; the traveller sees different roads.

The observer-relative partition belongs to the relation between observer and Library, not to an intrinsic alteration of the Library itself. The same static totality contains every possible path; the observer's coherence relation determines which paths are experienced as well-ordered and which as poorly ordered. The partition is a feature of the road the traveller walks, not of the ground beneath it.

The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) is a static, maximally complete, unbounded relational totality. It contains all configurations, all paths, all possible histories. It is unfiltered at the axiomatic level: membership in the Library does not imply persistence, coherence, observability, or accessibility. The Library may be infinite in cardinality, but coherence collapses indistinguishable copies into equivalence classes in the coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C := \mathcal{M} / \sim_C\). The Library itself is not intrinsically partitioned by the source construction or by any particular physical process.

The distinction between well-ordered and poorly ordered regions of the Library is not an intrinsic property of the Library. It is an observer-relative classification defined via the coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) and the continuous accessibility functional \(D_O(h,x,t)\). A configuration \(x \in \mathcal{M}\) is classified as well-ordered for observer \(O\) if the accessible distinguishability remains positive — that is, if \(D_O(h,x,t) > 0\) for all admissible \(t\). It is classified as poorly ordered if \(D_O\) reaches zero at the proposed coherence boundary — that is, if the accessible quotient has collapsed to a single equivalence class (or no accessible classes).

The structural statement at the boundary remains the discrete quotient condition \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) = 0\). The continuous accessibility functional \(D_O\) tracks the approach to that boundary and is the quantity that can carry a proposed power-law collapse rate. \(D_O\) and \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O)\) are related by the definitional interface: \(D_O = 0 \Leftrightarrow \dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) = 0\), and \(D_O > 0 \Leftrightarrow \dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) > 0\).

content.title: Well-Ordered vs. Poorly Ordered Regions (Observer-Relative Form)
content.text: Relative to an observer \(O\), the Library is partitioned as \(\mathcal{M} = \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O) \cup \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O)\), where \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O) = \{ x \in \mathcal{M} \mid D_O(h,x,t) > 0 \text{ for all admissible } t \text{ and the NSFG regularity conditions hold} \}\) and \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O) = \{ x \in \mathcal{M} \mid D_O(h,x,t) = 0 \text{ at the proposed coherence boundary, or the NSFG rupture condition is reached} \}\). These are observer-relative NSFG classifications; the underlying Library possesses no intrinsic classical partition.
content.latex: \forall O \in \operatorname{Obs}, \quad \mathcal{M} = \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O) \cup \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O); \quad \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O) = \{ x \in \mathcal{M} \mid D_O(h,x,t) > 0 \ \forall t \}; \quad \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O) = \{ x \in \mathcal{M} \mid D_O(h,x,t) = 0 \text{ at boundary} \}
content.interpretation: The distinction is defined via the continuous accessibility functional \(D_O\), with the discrete quotient dimension reserved for the structural boundary statement. Positive \(D_O\) corresponds to non-collapsed accessible distinguishability; \(D_O = 0\) corresponds to the proposed collapse state.

content.text: The well-ordered vs. poorly ordered distinction can also be expressed in terms of the coherence observables \(\Delta(t)\) and \(\mathcal{H}(t)\). A configuration is classified as well-ordered for observer \(O\) if the coherence phase remains below the critical threshold and the coherence hygiene remains finite: \(\Delta(x) < \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}\) and \(\mathcal{H}(x) < \infty\). It is classified as poorly ordered if the coherence phase exceeds the critical threshold or the coherence hygiene diverges: \(\Delta(x) \geq \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}\) or \(\mathcal{H}(x) = \infty\).

content.title: Well-Ordered vs. Poorly Ordered Regions (Coherence Variables Form)
content.text: The well-ordered region relative to observer \(O\) is \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O) = \{ x \in \mathcal{M} \mid \Delta(x) < \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}} \text{ and } \mathcal{H}(x) < \infty \}\). The poorly ordered region relative to observer \(O\) is \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O) = \{ x \in \mathcal{M} \mid \Delta(x) \geq \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}} \text{ or } \mathcal{H}(x) = \infty \}\). These are the coherence-variable criteria, equivalent to the \(D_O\)-form via the definitional interface.
content.interpretation: These are the coherence-variable criteria for the well-ordered vs. poorly ordered distinction. They are operationally equivalent to the \(D_O\)-form given the definitional interface stated above.

content.text: Within the proposed NSFG interpretation, the source construction is classified as entering the poorly ordered region. At \(t = 1\), the coherent continuation space \(\Gamma_O(h,x)\) is proposed to collapse to zero dimension: all coherent paths converge to a single equivalence class in \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\). This is the candidate Convergence Boundary interpretation of the source blow-up.

This classification is observer-relative. It is a claim about the observer's coherence relation to the Library, not about an intrinsic property of the Library. The Library itself remains unchanged. The continuous collapse behaviour is tracked by \(D_O\), while the structural statement at the boundary remains the discrete quotient condition \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) = 0\).

content.title: Candidate Location of the Source Construction (Observer-Relative Form)
content.text: Within the proposed NSFG interpretation, the source construction is classified as entering \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O)\). This classification is conditional on the Section 4.6 bridge lemmas B2 (Classical-to-NSFG Rupture) and B3 (Quotient Collapse). Until those lemmas are established, the location is an NSFG classification rather than a derived consequence.
content.latex: \text{Source construction} \in \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O) \quad \text{(candidate NSFG classification, conditional on Section 4.6 bridge)}
content.interpretation: The classification is proposed, not proven. It is observer-relative and conditional on the analytic bridge. It is a specific candidate path in the Library that crosses the coherence threshold, subject to the bridge lemmas.

content.text: Candidate smooth solutions, by contrast, are classified within the proposed NSFG interpretation as lying in \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O)\). For such a path, the coherence phase is proposed to remain below the critical threshold and the coherence hygiene is proposed to remain finite for all time: \(\Delta(t) < \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}\) and \(\mathcal{H}(t) < \infty\) for all \(t\). The accessible distinguishability \(D_O(h,x,t)\) is proposed to remain positive for all time, corresponding to \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) > 0\). Coherence is preserved.

content.title: Candidate Location of Smooth Solutions (Observer-Relative Form)
content.text: Within the proposed NSFG interpretation, smooth solutions are classified as lying in \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O)\). This classification is conditional on the Section 4.6 bridge: an NSFG-to-classical coercive lemma is required to promote the classification from an NSFG interpretation to a classical regularity statement.
content.latex: \text{Smooth solutions} \in \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O) \quad \text{(candidate NSFG classification, conditional on Section 4.6 bridge)}
content.interpretation: Smooth solutions are proposed to be paths in the Library that preserve coherence. They never cross the coherence threshold. The classification is conditional on the analytic bridge.

content.text: The observer-relative well-ordered vs. poorly ordered distinction offers an interpretation of the apparent tension between the source construction and the possibility of smooth solutions. The source construction is classified as a specific path in \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O)\). Candidate smooth solutions are classified as paths in \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O)\). They are different paths in the same static Library. The existence of a poorly ordered path does not preclude the existence of well-ordered paths. The Library contains both.

The classification is observer-relative. A configuration \(x \in \mathcal{M}\) may be classified as well-ordered for observer \(O_1\) and poorly ordered for observer \(O_2\), depending on their resolution thresholds \(I_N(O)\) and coherence conditions. This is because the accessibility functional \(D_O\) and the coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) depend on \(O\), \(h\), and \(x\). Different observers may have different quotient structures over the same Library.

content.title: Observer-Relativity of the Partition
content.text: There exist configurations \(x \in \mathcal{M}\) and observers \(O_1, O_2 \in \operatorname{Obs}\) such that \(x \in \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O_1)\) and \(x \in \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O_2)\). The classification depends on the observer's resolution threshold \(I_N(O)\), magnitude function \(\mu_O\), and coherence condition \(\mathcal{C}(\gamma \mid O,h,x)\).
content.interpretation: The partition is observer-relative. It is not an intrinsic classification of the Library. The same static totality contains every path; the observer's coherence relation determines which paths are experienced as well-ordered and which as poorly ordered.

content.title: Library Invariance Under the Observer-Relative Partition
content.text: The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) is the same static totality for every observer: for any two observers \(O_1, O_2\), the union \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O_i) \cup \mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O_i)\) is \(\mathcal{M}\) in both cases. The partition into well-ordered and poorly ordered regions is a feature of the observer's relation to the Library, not of the Library itself. The Library is not intrinsically partitioned by the source construction or by any particular physical process.
content.interpretation: The Library remains static and complete. The observer-relative partition is a classification of the observer's relation to the Library, not an intrinsic alteration of the Library.

content.title: Key Properties of the Observer-Relative Partition
items: The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) is static and complete; the partition is observer-relative.
Well-ordered relative to O: \(D_O(h,x,t) > 0\) for all admissible t; equivalently \(\Delta(t) < \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}\) and \(\mathcal{H}(t) < \infty\) for all t.
Poorly ordered relative to O: \(D_O(h,x,t) = 0\) at the proposed coherence boundary; equivalently \(\Delta(t) \geq \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}\) or \(\mathcal{H}(t) = \infty\).
The source construction is classified as entering \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O)\) as a candidate NSFG interpretation, conditional on the Section 4.6 bridge.
Candidate smooth solutions are classified as lying in \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{well}}(O)\), conditional on the same bridge.
The same configuration may be well-ordered for one observer and poorly ordered for another.
The distinction is defined via the continuous accessibility functional \(D_O\) and the coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\), not via an intrinsic property of the Library.
The structural boundary statement remains \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) = 0\); \(D_O\) tracks the continuous collapse amplitude.
Infinity exists in \(\mathcal{M}\) but is collapsed by coherence into equivalence classes in \(\mathcal{M}_C^O\).

content.text: The observer-relative partition is a direct consequence of the coherence quotient framework and the continuous accessibility functional \(D_O\). The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) may be infinite in cardinality, but the observer only experiences the coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) and the accessibility amplitude \(D_O\). When \(D_O\) remains positive, the observer experiences well-ordered structure. When \(D_O\) collapses to zero at the proposed coherence boundary, the observer experiences a poorly ordered region — a singularity. The source construction is classified as a specific instance of this general phenomenon, conditional on the Section 4.6 bridge.

content.title: Epistemic Status of the Partition and its Application
content.text: The observer-relative partition of the Library into well-ordered and poorly ordered regions is classified as \(D_{\text{translation hypothesis}}\). The application of the partition to the source construction — classifying it as a path in \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathrm{poor}}(O)\) — is likewise classified as \(D_{\text{translation hypothesis}}\), conditional on the Section 4.6 bridge lemmas. The promotion condition requires the establishment of the Section 4.6 bridge lemmas B2 and B3, along with an explicit formula for \(D_O\) in terms of \(\psi\), \(\Phi\), \(A\), and \(I_N(O)\), and proofs of continuity and monotonicity of \(D_O\) along admissible paths.

content.interpretation: The partition is a proposed NSFG classification, not a derived consequence of the source construction. The classification is conditional on the analytic bridge. The promotion condition identifies the specific mathematical obligations required to strengthen it.

content.title: Definition 7.1 — Coherence as the Substrate of Physics
content.text: Physics is not about matter, energy, or fields as primitives. It is about coherence—the persistence of meaning through recursive transformation. The fundamental objects are distinctions (XOR), the Library \(\mathcal{M}\) (the totality of all possible distinctions), and coherence \(\mathcal{C}(\gamma \mid O,h,x)\) (the relation that determines which distinctions survive for a given observer).
content.interpretation: The objects of physics—matter, energy, fields, spacetime—are emergent regularities of coherence-preserving traversal through \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\). They are not primitives. The OpenAI construction is a proof that coherence can rupture, demonstrating that smoothness is conditional on coherence preservation.

content.text: This reframing has profound implications for how we understand physical law. In standard physics, laws are assumed to be universal and observer-independent. In NSFG, laws are emergent regularities of observer-relative coherence. Different observers may experience different regularities, depending on their resolution threshold \(I_N(O)\), their coherence relation \(\mathcal{C}(\gamma \mid O,h,x)\), and their position in the Library. This does not mean that physics is arbitrary—it means that physics is relational.

The OpenAI construction is a specific instance of this relational structure. The blow-up at t=1 corresponds to a coherence rupture: the motif braid \(\Delta(t)\) crosses its critical threshold \(\Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}\), and the long-horizon coherence \(\mathcal{H}(t)\) diverges. The symbolic identity of the flow is lost. The OpenAI construction proves that coherence can rupture in the Navier-Stokes equations. NSFG explains why this rupture occurs: it is a Convergence Boundary in the observer-relative coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\).

content.text: what is conserved is not energy — but the meaning that structures it

Coherence conservation is the preservation of positive quotient dimension \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) > 0\). When coherence is conserved, the observer-relative accessible quotient remains structurally rich. When coherence ruptures, the dimension collapses to 0, and the system can no longer maintain structure — this is the NSFG interpretation of blow-up.

The NSFG framework suggests that coherence is a conserved quantity in physical systems. When coherence is lost, the system can no longer maintain structure, and blow-up occurs. This is a new conservation law, distinct from energy, momentum, and angular momentum. It provides a new way to understand physical systems.

In classical physics, conservation laws are statements about quantities that remain invariant under time evolution: energy, momentum, angular momentum, and (in certain contexts) charge or mass. These quantities are defined on the classical state space — the space of velocity fields, pressure fields, and their derivatives. Coherence conservation is a statement about the observer-relative accessible quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\), not about the classical state space directly.

The coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) is the set of equivalence classes distinguishable by observer O from history h and reference x. Its dimension \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x))\) is the number of coherently distinguishable equivalence classes available to the observer. Coherence conservation is the preservation of this dimension: \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x))\) remains positive and constant in well-ordered regions. Coherence rupture is the collapse of this dimension to 0 in poorly ordered regions.

The specific value of the dimension may vary, but it does not collapse to 0. This is a structural conservation law: it is about the preservation of distinguishability, not about the preservation of a numerical quantity.

When this occurs, the observer can no longer distinguish between paths. This is the NSFG interpretation of the OpenAI blow-up: \(\Delta(t) \to \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}\) or \(\mathcal{H}(t) \to \infty\) corresponds to \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) \to 0\).

In quotient terms, \(\dim(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) \to 0\): the observer-relative accessible quotient collapses to a single equivalence class. This is the Convergence Boundary singularity.

content.title: Coherence Conservation is Distinct from Classical Conservation Laws
content.text: Coherence conservation does not imply energy conservation, momentum conservation, or angular momentum conservation. A system may conserve coherence while exchanging energy, momentum, or angular momentum with its environment. Conversely, a system may conserve energy while losing coherence. This distinguishes coherence from classical conserved quantities.
content.interpretation: Coherence conservation is a structural conservation law, not a numerical one. It is about the preservation of distinguishability in the accessible quotient, not about the preservation of a numerical quantity in the classical state space.

content.text: the Library is not a model — it is the structure from which all models emerge

The Library 𝓜 is the ultimate substrate of all physical systems. It contains all possible configurations, all possible paths, all possible laws. The Navier-Stokes equations are one set of paths in the Library. The OpenAI construction is one of those paths — specifically, a path in 𝓜_poor where coherence collapses to a single equivalence class in \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\). Smooth solutions lie in 𝓜_well, where the coherence quotient retains positive dimension.

The Library 𝓜 is the XOR closure of the formal domain \(D\): \(\mathcal{M} := \operatorname{Closure}_D(\oplus, G)\). It is a static, maximally complete, unbounded relational totality with full adjacency and no privileged exterior. It contains all configurations that are internally describable — coherent and incoherent, accessible and inaccessible, physical and non-physical. Membership in the Library is independent of any observer's resolution or coherence condition.

The Navier-Stokes equations are one set of paths in this Library: \(\operatorname{NS}(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,\infty)) \subset \mathcal{M}\). Every Navier-Stokes solution corresponds to a path through the Library. The equations themselves are an emergent regularity — a pattern in the Library that persists for certain paths. The OpenAI construction is one such path.

The Library is partitioned by coherence into two regions: \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{well}}\) and \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{poor}}\). This partition is defined at the level of the coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\), not at the level of \(\mathcal{M}\). The coherence quotient is the set of equivalence classes distinguishable by observer \(O\) from history \(h\) and reference \(x\). The partition depends on the observer's resolution threshold \(I_N(O)\) and coherence condition \(\mathcal{C}(\gamma \mid O,h,x)\).

The OpenAI construction is a specific path in \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{poor}}\). At \(t = 1\), the accessible quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) collapses to zero dimension — all coherent paths converge to a single equivalence class. This is the Convergence Boundary singularity (PHYS-CORE-013 §4.2). The infinity of possible histories in \(\mathcal{M}\) collapses to a single distinguishable class for the observer. The Library itself remains unchanged; the collapse is observer-relative and coherence-based.

Smooth Navier-Stokes solutions correspond to paths in \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{well}}\). In \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{well}}\), coherence is preserved: \(\Delta(t) < \Delta_{\text{crit}}\) and \(\mathcal{H}(t) < \infty\) for all \(t \geq 0\). The accessible quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) retains positive dimension — the observer can distinguish multiple equivalence classes. The path continues coherently without reaching a Convergence Boundary.

The OpenAI construction and smooth solutions are therefore different paths in the same Library. The OpenAI construction is a proof of concept for coherence rupture — it shows that there exist paths in \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{poor}}\) where coherence collapses. Smooth solutions show that there exist paths in \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{well}}\) where coherence is preserved. Both are compatible because they are different paths in the same static totality.

This is a structural property: the Library has no privileged boundary or terminal configuration. It does not imply infinite cardinality, but it is compatible with it. The unboundedness of \(\mathcal{M}\) is independent of any observer's coherence quotient.

content.title: Key Properties of the Library as Substrate
items: The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) is the XOR closure of \(D\): \(\mathcal{M} := \operatorname{Closure}_D(\oplus, G)\).
The Library is static, complete, unbounded, and relationally complete.
The Library is unfiltered: membership does not imply persistence, coherence, observability, or accessibility.
Navier-Stokes paths are a subset of \(\mathcal{M}\): \(\operatorname{NS}(\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0,\infty)) \subset \mathcal{M}\).
The coherence quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C := \mathcal{M} / \sim_C\) defines the set of coherence-distinguishable equivalence classes.
The observer-relative quotient \(\mathcal{M}_C^O := \mathcal{M} / \sim_O\) defines the classes distinguishable by observer \(O\).
The partition \(\mathcal{M} = \mathcal{M}_{\text{well}} \cup \mathcal{M}_{\text{poor}}\) is defined at the quotient level, not at the Library level.
The OpenAI construction is a path in \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{poor}}\): \(\gamma_{\text{OpenAI}} \in \mathcal{M}_{\text{poor}}\).
Smooth solutions are paths in \(\mathcal{M}_{\text{well}}\): \(\gamma_{\text{smooth}} \in \mathcal{M}_{\text{well}}\).
The OpenAI construction and smooth solutions are compatible because they are different paths in the same Library.
The Library is unbounded: \(\forall x \in \mathcal{M}, \exists y \in \mathcal{M}\) distinguishable from \(x\) under some observer condition.
The Library is invariant under coherence collapse: \(\mathcal{M}\) remains \(\mathcal{M}\) even when \(\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\) collapses.

content.title: What This Paper Establishes, Proposes, and Predicts
items: **Establishes (source-supported).** The supplied OpenAI manuscript presents a specific forced finite-time Navier–Stokes blow-up construction with stated scaling laws (as given in the source).

**Establishes (structural).** PHYS-CORE-014 supplies an NSFG translation architecture: a mapping table from source variables to NSFG coherence variables, with each row carrying an explicit epistemic status (Section 3; Appendix A).

**Identifies (bridge obligations).** Section 4.6 identifies the exact analytic lemmas (B1–B3) required to convert the NSFG interpretation into a rigorous conditional correspondence between the source blow-up and a candidate NSFG coherence rupture.
**Interprets.** Within the proposed NSFG framework, the source blow-up path is interpreted as a candidate Convergence Boundary in the observer-relative coherence quotient \mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x).

**Predicts (conditional).** NSFG predicts a family of candidate rupture paths parameterized by an exponent \alpha > 0, with corresponding classical velocity scaling |u| \asymp \tau^{-(\alpha + 1/2)} if the required translation bridge is established.

**Predicts (conditional).** NSFG predicts a continuous collapse law D_O \asymp \tau^{\gamma} for observer-relative accessible distinguishability along a rupture path, with \gamma determined by the path and by the explicit D_O definition.
**Conjectures.** The Coherence Rupture Classification Theorem remains conjectural pending the missing bridge results.
**Conjectures.** The coherence-preservation regularity criterion remains conditional on the same bridge lemmas.

The source supplies the classical blow-up path; NSFG supplies the structural vocabulary in which that path can be described as a candidate coherence rupture, and it makes the analytic bridge obligations explicit. content.text: Together, the source construction and the NSFG framework point toward a reframing of physics as the study of coherence — the persistence of meaning through recursive transformation. The Library \mathcal{M} may be infinite in cardinality, but coherence collapses indistinguishability into equivalence classes in \mathcal{M}_C^O. The candidate singularity is where that collapse becomes maximal. This reframing is a structural interpretation, not a completed proof of global regularity or of universal blow-up.

This identification is a translation hypothesis (D); the corresponding classical-to-NSFG and NSFG-to-classical implications require bridge lemmas B1–B3, which are currently unproved.

The answer is: it can be interpreted structurally as a candidate Convergence Boundary, provided the analytic bridge lemmas identified in Section 4.6 are established. The framework does not avoid singularities; it describes them as structural effects of maximal constraint on coherent traversal. The map is drawn; the crossing remains to be built.

subsections.title: Definition of Φ
subsections.purpose: To give the exact tensor/scalar definition of Φ used in the coherence hygiene functional ℋ and to specify its relation to the coherence potential ψ and the swirl torsion vector potential A.
subsections.poetic_cipher: Name the object before you measure it.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The coherence hygiene functional ℋ is defined in terms of Φ, but Φ must first be defined. This subsection closes that obligation.

content.text: The swirl curvature tensor Φ is the object whose second derivatives enter the definition of ℋ. It is defined from the coherence potential ψ and the swirl torsion vector potential A appearing in the Helmholtz decomposition u = ∇ψ + ∇×A. The definition given here is the NSFG internal definition; its relation to the classical velocity field is a translation hypothesis, not a derivation.

content.title: Definition 9.2.1 — Swirl Curvature Tensor Φ
content.text: The swirl curvature tensor Φ is defined as the second covariant derivative of the coherence potential ψ, plus the curl of the swirl torsion vector potential A contracted once with the coherence frame. Explicitly, in the NSFG internal coordinates: Φ_{μν} := ∂_μ ∂_ν ψ + (∂_μ A_ν - ∂_ν A_μ) + κ_{μν}(M), where κ_{μν}(M) is a correction term determined by the motif frame M. The correction term vanishes on the flat-frame reference configuration used in the source-comparison setting.
content.interpretation: Φ encodes the local curvature of the coherence structure. Its second derivatives enter ℋ. The correction term κ_{μν}(M) vanishes in the frame in which the source construction is analyzed.

content.text: When A = 0 (purely irrotational flow), Φ reduces to the Hessian of ψ. When ψ is linear (uniform coherence potential) and A carries the swirl, Φ reduces to the curl of A. The general form is the sum of both contributions.

subsections.title: Construction of Φ from u
subsections.purpose: To specify whether Φ is uniquely determined by the classical velocity field u and to state the gauge or decomposition choices required for a well-defined construction.
subsections.poetic_cipher: Two field variables, one classical input, and a choice that must be named.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The Helmholtz decomposition u = ∇ψ + ∇×A is not unique without gauge and boundary conditions. This subsection names the choices.

content.text: The Helmholtz decomposition u = ∇ψ + ∇×A requires gauge choices. On ℝ³ with the standard decay conditions, the decomposition is unique if we require ∇·A = 0 and decay of ψ and A at infinity. On a bounded domain or on the torus, additional boundary conditions are required. On the source construction on ℝ³, the standard gauge ∇·A = 0 may be assumed, but the paper must verify that the source construction satisfies the decay conditions required for uniqueness.

content.title: Construction 9.2.2 — Φ from u
content.text: Given a smooth divergence-free velocity field u on the source domain, define ψ and A by the Helmholtz decomposition u = ∇ψ + ∇×A subject to the gauge ∇·A = 0 and the decay conditions required for uniqueness on the domain. Then Φ is constructed from ψ and A by the definition in 9.2.1. The construction is a translation hypothesis: the existence and uniqueness of the required (ψ, A) pair on the source domain is an analytic obligation.
content.interpretation: The construction is well-defined on domains where the Helmholtz decomposition with the stated gauge is unique. Establishing that the source construction's domain admits such a decomposition is an open obligation.

content.title: Open Obligations for the Construction
items: Verify that the source construction's domain (ℝ³ × [0,T)) admits a Helmholtz decomposition with the stated gauge.
Verify that ψ and A decay sufficiently at infinity for the decomposition to be unique.
Establish that the resulting Φ has the regularity required for ℋ to be well-defined.

content.text: A proof that the Helmholtz decomposition with gauge ∇·A = 0 and the required decay conditions is unique on the source domain, together with the required regularity of ψ and A, would promote this construction to C_derived.

subsections.title: Direct Scaling Derivation of ℋ
subsections.purpose: To derive the scaling ℋ(t) ≍ τ^{-1/2-3h} directly from the scaling of Φ, the spatial derivative scaling, and the shrinking support volume, without using inequality reversal.
subsections.epistemic_status: D_translation_hypothesis; promotion to C_derived requires completion of the derivation below
subsections.poetic_cipher: Integrate the square of the curvature over the shrinking volume.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The scaling of ℋ is the product of three factors: the amplitude of ∇²Φ squared, and the volume of its support. Each factor must be derived from source-supported scaling, not asserted.

content.text: The coherence hygiene functional is ℋ(t) = ∫_Ω |∇²Φ(x,t)|² dx. Its scaling is determined by three factors: (i) the amplitude of ∇²Φ in the support region; (ii) the volume of the support region at time t; (iii) the rate at which the support region shrinks as τ → 0.

content.title: Scaling Derivation 9.2.3 — From Φ to ℋ
content.text: Assume the following source-supported or NSFG-defined scalings: (a) the support of Φ at time t has radial extent ℓ_r ≍ τ^{1/2} and axial extent ℓ_z ≍ τ^{1/2-h}, so its volume scales as V(t) ≍ ℓ_r² ℓ_z ≍ τ^{1-h}; (b) the amplitude of ∇²Φ scales as A_{∇²Φ}(t) ≍ τ^{-1/2-h}. Then ℋ(t) ≍ A_{∇²Φ}(t)² · V(t) ≍ τ^{-1-2h} · τ^{1-h} = τ^{-3h}. This yields the scaling ℋ(t) ≍ τ^{-3h}.
content.interpretation: The direct integration yields ℋ(t) ≍ τ^{-3h}, which differs from the previously asserted ℋ(t) ≍ τ^{-1/2-3h}. The discrepancy indicates either that the amplitude scaling of ∇²Φ is different from τ^{-1/2-h}, or that the volume scaling of the support is different from τ^{1-h}, or both. The exact scaling of ℋ requires the amplitude and volume scalings to be derived directly from the source construction.

content.title: Open Obligation
content.text: The amplitude scaling of ∇²Φ and the volume scaling of its support must be derived directly from the source construction. Until this is done, the scaling of ℋ cannot be asserted. The value ℋ(t) ≍ τ^{-1/2-3h} that appears in the current draft of PHYS-CORE-014 is not consistent with the amplitude and volume scalings used here, and must be replaced by a derivation-specific value or flagged as unverified.
content.latex: \text{Until } A_{\nabla^2\Phi}(t) \text{ and } V(t) \text{ are derived from the source, the scaling of } \mathcal{H}(t) \text{ is an open obligation.}

content.text: The following dimensional audit verifies the consistency of the primary NSFG quantities and the proposed mappings. Where a dimension is not yet determined, the obligation is stated explicitly.

rows.Notes: Matches the dimension of the source angular Reynolds rate \mathrm{Re}_\theta / L^2 · \nu up to constants. Confirmation requires the promotion of \Delta \asymp \mathrm{Re}_\theta.
\Delta_{\mathrm{crit}} = \epsilon_N (\nu/L^2)^{1/2}; with \epsilon_N dimensionless and \nu/L^2 in T^{-2}, the square root is T^{-1}.

ℋ = ∫_Ω |∇²Φ|² dx. If Φ has dimension L² (curvature), ∇²Φ has dimension L^{-2}·L² = L^0, which is dimensionless, and ℋ has dimension L^3 (volume). This is inconsistent with the scaling \mathcal{H} \asymp \tau^{-1/2-3h} unless Φ has a different dimension. The dimension of Φ must be specified.
Dimensionless. Determined by the observer's resolution threshold.
The dimension of ψ must be chosen so that ∇ψ has the dimension of velocity (L T^{-1}). This gives [ψ] = L² T^{-1}, consistent with the irrotational component of the Helmholtz decomposition.
The dimension of A must be chosen so that ∇×A has the dimension of velocity. This gives [A] = L² T^{-1}, the same as ψ.

rows.Status: A_definition; dimension to be confirmed by consistency
rows.Notes: If Φ is the sum of ∂_μ∂_νψ and ∂_μA_ν - ∂_νA_μ, then ∂_μ∂_νψ has dimension L^{-1}·L² T^{-1} = L T^{-1} and ∂_μA_ν has dimension L^{-1}·L² T^{-1} = L T^{-1}. Both contributions have the same dimension.

rows.Status: A_definition; dimension proposed to ensure pressure consistency
rows.Notes: For p = ∇ψ · ζ to have dimension ML^{-1}T^{-2}, with [∇ψ] = L T^{-1}, we need [ζ] = ML^{-2}T^{-1}. This specification is currently pending.

subsections.title: Definition of D_O
subsections.purpose: To formally define the continuous accessibility functional D_O(h,x,t) used in the continuous scaling laws of Sections 5.3 and 6.1, distinguishing it from the discrete/topological quotient dimension dim(ℳ_C^O).
subsections.epistemic_status: A_definition within NSFG; explicit formula is an open specification task
subsections.poetic_cipher: Do not make the number of doors into the width of a door.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The number or dimension of accessible directions is structural; the degree of remaining accessibility is continuous. D_O measures the latter without pretending that dimension itself varies fractionally.

content.text: The continuous accessibility functional D_O is introduced to represent the degree of observer-relative accessible distinguishability at a configuration (h,x) at time t. It is distinct from the discrete/topological quotient dimension dim(ℳ_C^O(h,x)), which remains an integer-valued structural quantity. D_O is the continuous amplitude whose collapse is tracked by the power-law predictions in Sections 5.3 and 6.1.

content.title: Definition 9.2.6 — Continuous Accessibility Functional D_O
content.text: The continuous accessibility functional is a nonnegative real-valued function D_O : H_O × ℳ_admissible × [0,T) → ℝ_{≥0}, where H_O is the observer-relative history space, ℳ_admissible is the admissible reference configuration set, and [0,T) is the physical time domain. It satisfies the following constraints: (i) D_O(h,x,t) ≥ 0 for all (h,x,t); (ii) D_O(h,x,t) = 0 represents the proposed collapse state, corresponding to dim(ℳ_C^O(h,x)) = 0; (iii) D_O(h,x,t) > 0 represents non-collapsed accessible distinguishability; (iv) D_O is continuous in t along any admissible path γ ∈ Γ_O(h,x); (v) D_O is monotone non-increasing along a rupture path, meaning that along a path that eventually reaches a Convergence Boundary, D_O is non-increasing in t; (vi) D_O satisfies the consistency condition with dim(ℳ_C^O): D_O = 0 ⇒ dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0, and D_O > 0 ⇒ dim(ℳ_C^O) > 0.
content.interpretation: D_O is the continuous amplitude whose collapse to zero corresponds to the structural collapse of the accessibility quotient. It is defined by its properties; its explicit formula in terms of ψ, Φ, and A is an open specification task.

content.title: Open Obligations for D_O
items: Provide an explicit formula for D_O in terms of ψ, Φ, A, and I_N(O).
Prove that D_O = 0 if and only if the boundary condition dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0 is reached.
Prove continuity of D_O in t along admissible paths.
Prove monotonicity of D_O along rupture paths.
Specify the normalization of D_O (e.g., whether D_O is bounded above by 1 or unbounded above).

content.title: Relation to the Discrete Quotient Dimension
content.text: The functional D_O and the discrete dimension dim(ℳ_C^O) are consistent but not identical. The consistency condition D_O = 0 ⇔ dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0 ensures that collapse in the continuous functional corresponds to structural collapse in the discrete quotient. The functional D_O may vary continuously between positive values while dim(ℳ_C^O) remains constant at a fixed positive integer. The functional D_O is the object to which continuous power laws such as D_O ≍ τ^γ apply.

content.title: Promotion Condition
content.text: A proof that the functional D_O as defined satisfies the consistency condition with dim(ℳ_C^O), together with an explicit formula in terms of ψ, Φ, and A, would promote the definition to a fully specified NSFG observable.
content.latex: \text{Promotion requires an explicit formula for } D_O \text{ and a proof of the consistency condition.}

content.text: This appendix establishes the NSFG coherence rupture criterion as a definition within the NSFG framework, exposes the bridge obligations required to promote it to a classical correspondence, and defines the continuous accessibility functional D_O used in the continuous scaling laws of Sections 5.3 and 6.1. The appendix does not claim that the correspondence to classical blow-up has been proved. The correspondence is conditional on the bridge lemmas B1–B3 identified in Section 4.6 of the main text.

The structure of this appendix is as follows. Subsection 9.2.1 defines the swirl curvature tensor Φ. Subsection 9.2.2 specifies the construction of Φ from the classical velocity u. Subsection 9.2.3 derives the scaling of ℋ directly from the scaling of Φ, the spatial derivative scaling, and the shrinking support volume, without using inequality reversal. Subsection 9.2.4 states the direction of each proposed bridge inequality. Subsection 9.2.5 audits the dimensional consistency of the primary NSFG observables and proposed mappings. Subsection 9.2.6 defines the continuous accessibility functional D_O.

content.title: Summary: What This Appendix Establishes
content.text: The NSFG coherence rupture criterion is defined by Δ(t) ≥ Δ_crit and/or ℋ(t) → ∞. This is a definition within NSFG. The proposed correspondence between this criterion and the classical blow-up condition is a translation hypothesis conditional on the bridge lemmas B1–B3. The correspondence between this criterion and the Convergence Boundary condition is a translation hypothesis conditional on the Quotient Collapse Lemma B3. The continuous accessibility functional D_O is defined by its properties; its explicit formula is an open specification task. No triple equivalence is claimed as proved in v0.1.1.
content.latex: \text{NSFG rupture} \;:=\; \Delta(t) \geq \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}} \text{ OR } \mathcal{H}(t) \to \infty \quad (\text{A_definition}); \\ \text{NSFG rupture} \Rightarrow \text{Convergence Boundary} \quad (\text{D_translation_hypothesis, conditional on B3}); \\ \text{NSFG rupture} \Rightarrow \text{classical blow-up} \quad (\text{E_prediction_or_conjecture, conditional on B1--B3}).
content.interpretation: The appendix presents an NSFG-internal definition, a proposed structural correspondence, and a conjectural classical correspondence. It separates these three epistemic levels explicitly so that no unsupported equivalence is asserted.

content.text: the rupture is the collapse of accessibility, not of the number of doors

Coherence rupture is a collapse of observer-relative accessible distinguishability within the coherence quotient. When the continuous accessibility functional D_O drops to zero, all coherent paths converge to a single equivalence class — this is the proposed Convergence Boundary singularity. The number of doors (dim(ℳ_C^O)) remains structural; what collapses is the width of access through them. The source blow-up is interpreted as a physical manifestation of this accessibility collapse, conditional on the bridge lemmas of Section 4.6.

The correspondence to classical blow-up remains conditional on the bridge lemmas B1–B3 identified in Section 4.6.

The classification is explicitly an NSFG prediction; the existence of classical solutions realizing each α must be established independently.

subsections.special_considerations: This appendix establishes the NSFG coherence rupture criterion as a definition, exposes the bridge obligations required to promote it to a classical correspondence, and defines the continuous accessibility functional D_O. It corrects the following errors from the previous version: (a) it does not assert the triple equivalence as proved; (b) it distinguishes the threshold crossing time τ_crit = (C/Δ_crit)^{1/h} from the singular limit τ → 0; (c) it derives the scaling of ℋ from the scaling of Φ and the support volume, and identifies that the previously asserted exponent τ^{-1/2-3h} is not consistent with the amplitude and volume scalings used and must be re-derived; (d) it lists every bridge inequality with its permitted direction and prohibits inequality reversal; (e) it audits dimensional consistency and identifies open obligations for Φ, ζ, and D_O; (f) it defines D_O as the continuous amplitude whose collapse is tracked by power laws, reserving dim(ℳ_C^O) for the discrete/topological quotient dimension. The handoff to Section 9.3 preserves the distinction between NSFG definitions, translation hypotheses, and predictions.

content.text: The OpenAI construction is a specific source-supported classical blow-up construction. It is not an isolated anomaly, but it is also not a universal theorem. This appendix classifies the family of candidate coherence rupture paths in NSFG, parameterized by the scaling exponent α > 0, and locates the source construction as one source-supported path within this family.

The classification is grounded in the coherence quotient framework established in Appendix A and the mapping established in Appendix B. Three distinct classes of claim must be kept separate: (i) the source-supported classical content established by the OpenAI manuscript under its stated hypotheses; (ii) the NSFG prediction family parameterized by α > 0; (iii) the universal rupture classification, which remains conjectural pending bridge lemmas B1–B3 from Section 4.6.

content.title: General Candidate Coherence Rupture Path
content.text: An NSFG candidate coherence rupture path is parameterized by a scaling exponent α > 0: Δ(t) ≍ τ^{-α}. The proposed associated scalings are |u| ≍ τ^{-(α + 1/2)} for the classical velocity and ℋ(t) ≍ τ^{-(2α + 1/2)} for the coherence hygiene. These are NSFG predictions, not classical theorems, until the bridge lemmas are established.
content.interpretation: The exponent α parameterizes the rate at which coherence phase pressure is proposed to diverge. Larger α corresponds to faster candidate rupture. The structural outcome is proposed to be the same for all α: a candidate Convergence Boundary in ℳ_C^O.

content.title: Epistemic Status of the α-Family
content.text: The α-family is classified as E_prediction_or_conjecture. It is an NSFG prediction, not a family of already-constructed classical solutions. Each member of the family requires: (i) an explicit NSFG construction producing Δ_α(t) with the stated scaling; (ii) a classical realization constructed independently; (iii) verification of the bridge lemmas B1–B3 for that member. Without these, the α-family states what NSFG predicts, not what has been proven.
content.interpretation: A scaling prediction is not an existence theorem. The α-family specifies the shape of candidate paths without constructing classical solutions that travel them.

content.text: The source construction is classified as B_classical_or_source_result on the classical side and as D_translation_hypothesis on the NSFG side. Its velocity and velocity-gradient scalings are source-supported classical facts. Its identification with the NSFG parameter α = h is a translation hypothesis. Its identification with a candidate Convergence Boundary is a D_translation_hypothesis requiring the Quotient Collapse Lemma B3.

content.interpretation: The limit α → 0+ is a candidate boundary between Convergence Boundaries and the XOR Fixed Point within the NSFG taxonomy. It is not a constructed solution.

content.text: The classification establishes that the source construction is one source-supported classical path receiving an NSFG interpretation. The α-family is an NSFG prediction whose existence and scaling properties require independent construction and the bridge lemmas B1–B3. The universal rupture classification remains conjectural. The distinctions between these classes are maintained throughout this appendix to prevent the existence of one construction from being silently generalized into a universal theorem.
One footprint proves one traveller.

content.text: the Library has no poor regions; the observer does

The Library \\(\\mathcal{M}\\) is not divided into well-ordered and poorly ordered regions. The distinction arises in the observer's relation to the Library, tracked by the continuous accessibility functional \\(D_O(h,x,t)\\). When \\(D_O > 0\\), the observer retains coherently distinguishable structure; when \\(D_O \\to 0\\), accessibility collapses toward the proposed coherence boundary. The Library itself remains static and complete throughout.

This appendix records the observer-relative classification of the Library that underlies the interpretation of the source OpenAI construction. It does not claim that the Library itself contains intrinsic well-ordered and poorly ordered regions. The classification is a feature of the observer's relation to the Library, expressed through the coherence quotient \\(\\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)\\) and the continuous accessibility functional \\(D_O(h,x,t)\\).

The partition is expressed using D_O rather than the structural quotient dimension \\(\\dim(\\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x))\\). The structural dimension is a discrete and topological quantity; it is not assigned a continuous power-law. D_O is the continuous amplitude whose collapse is tracked by predicted power laws such as \\(D_O \\asymp \\tau^{\\gamma}\\). The defining constraint relating the two is \\(D_O = 0 \\Rightarrow \\dim(\\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) = 0\\) and \\(D_O > 0 \\Rightarrow \\dim(\\mathcal{M}_C^O(h,x)) > 0\\), with the converse direction reserved as an open obligation in Section 9.2.6.

The observer-relative partition into \\(\\mathfrak{M}_{\\text{well}}(O)\\) and \\(\\mathfrak{M}_{\\text{poor}}(O)\\) is a definition within NSFG. Its use to classify classical Navier-Stokes solutions as smooth or singular is a D_translation_hypothesis: the identification of the well-ordered region with classical global smoothness, and of the poorly ordered region with classical finite-time blow-up, requires the Section 4.6 bridge lemmas and is not asserted as proven here.

content.title: The Five Epistemic Status Labels
items: **A_definition** — A definition internal to NSFG or adopted from an explicitly cited source. May be used for new symbols, new functionals, and adopted standard definitions. May not be used for empirical claims, analytic equivalences, or existence assertions.

**B_classical_or_source_result** — A result actually established in the cited mathematical source under its stated hypotheses. May be used for results as stated in the source. May not be used for consequences not shown in the source or for generalizations of the source.

**C_derived** — A mathematical consequence derived from definitions and already-established results, with all required hypotheses shown. May be used for lemmas with full proofs and corollaries with explicit hypotheses. May not be used for results whose proofs rely on unproved bridges or whose hypotheses are not yet verified.

**D_translation_hypothesis** — A proposed NSFG-to-classical or classical-to-NSFG correspondence whose analytic equivalence has not yet been independently established. May be used for mappings between frameworks and conjectural identifications of quantities. May not be used for statements presented as proven equivalences.

**E_prediction_or_conjecture** — A claim proposed by NSFG that requires a new proof, construction, or empirical/mathematical validation. May be used for generalized scaling families, universal classification theorems, and falsifiable predictions. May not be used for results presented as consequences of the axioms alone.

The central claim of the conditional equivalence between the OpenAI Navier-Stokes blow-up and the NSFG Convergence Boundary relies on three unproved bridge lemmas identified in Section 4.6. To facilitate the mathematical labor required to promote these hypotheses from `E_prediction_or_conjecture` to `C_derived`, this appendix outlines the necessary proof architectures. content.title: Architecture for Lemma B1: Coercive NSFG-to-Classical Lemma

Since predicting classical blow-up from a structural framework requires a coercive lower estimate, the proof must be constructed via contrapositive using established classical regularity theorems.

content.text: Lemma B2 is the most immediately tractable of the three, as it deals directly with the explicit construction provided by the OpenAI manuscript. The goal is to prove that the classical blow-up specifically forces the NSFG variables to cross their critical thresholds. An upper bound is insufficient; we must establish a rigorous lower bound that survives spatial integration.

content.title: Architecture for Lemma B2: Classical-to-NSFG Rupture Lemma
content.text: Objective: Prove that the specific classical blow-up described by the OpenAI construction forces an NSFG coherence rupture. This requires demonstrating a coercive lower bound on the coherence phase pressure $\Delta(t)$ directly from the similarity profiles.

content.title: Proof Steps for Lemma B2
items: **Step 1: Extract Source Profiles.** Take the explicit self-similar profiles $E(X,\eta)$, $U(X,\eta)$, and $\Pi(X,\eta)$ constructed in the OpenAI manuscript (Sections 4 and 5).

**Step 2: Isolate the Irrotational Component.** Apply the Helmholtz decomposition to the localized core velocity $u^{(0)}$. Because the OpenAI core is highly structured and axisymmetric, write down the explicit integral representation for the coherence potential $\psi(x,t)$ within the active annulus.
**Step 3: Construct the Swirl Tensor.** Form the tensor $\Phi$ directly from $\psi$ and the residual vector potential $A$.

**Step 4: Establish the Lower Bound.** Calculate the time derivative $\partial_t \Phi(x,t)$. By focusing evaluation on the specific spatial trajectory $X = X_{\mathrm{in}}$, use the positivity of the source amplitude $e_0$ to establish a rigorous lower bound: $\sup_x |\partial_t \Phi| \geq c_0 \tau^{-h}$ for some absolute constant $c_0 > 0$.

**Step 5: Threshold Crossing.** Given finite $\Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}$, demonstrate that $c_0 \tau^{-h}$ strictly exceeds $\Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}$ at a finite positive remaining time $\tau_{\mathrm{crit}} > 0$.

content.text: Lemma B3 bridges the gap between the purely analytical condition of NSFG rupture (the divergence of $\Delta$ or $\mathcal{H}$) and the deep ontological claim of NSFG: that the observer-relative accessible quotient $\mathcal{M}_C^O$ collapses to zero dimension. This proof must operate entirely within the axiomatic floor of NSFG. The detailed architecture for B3 is provided in subsection 9.6.B3 below.

content.title: Concluding Remark on the Architectures
content.text: These proof architectures isolate the mathematical domains required for the completion of the correspondence. Lemma B1 requires classical PDE expertise (Sobolev embeddings, elliptic regularity). Lemma B2 requires direct asymptotic analysis of the similarity profiles provided by the OpenAI manuscript. Lemma B3 requires structural logic and relational topology based on the NSFG primer. Discharging these three obligations is the required path to promoting the conditional framework to a complete theorem.

math.label: Lemma B1 (Coercive NSFG-to-Classical) — Formal Statement
math.expression: \text{If } \mathcal{H}(t) \to \infty \text{ or } \Delta(t) \to \infty \text{ as } t \to T^*, \text{ then } \limsup_{t \to T^*} \|u(t)\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)} = \infty \text{ or } \limsup_{t \to T^*} \|\nabla u(t)\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)} = \infty
assumptions: The NSFG translation layer is assumed to be well-defined (see Lemma B2 architecture for the forward direction).
The coercive estimate is required; an upper bound alone is insufficient.
The proof proceeds by contraposition of an established classical regularity criterion.

math.label: Contrapositive of BKM Criterion
assumptions: The Beale-Kato-Majda criterion is established: a smooth Euler or Navier-Stokes solution continues past time T^* if the time-integral of the L^∞ norm of vorticity is finite.
The contrapositive states: if the solution does not continue past T^*, then the time-integral of vorticity is infinite.

proof_architecture.strategy: Contrapositive via classical regularity criterion (BKM). Assume classical global regularity and derive boundedness of the NSFG coherence observables.

steps.title: Contrapositive Framing
steps.content: Assume, for contradiction, that the classical velocity field u(x,t) remains globally regular on ℝ³ × [0, T^*) and satisfies the Beale-Kato-Majda criterion: ∫_0^{T^*} ||ω(t)||_{L^∞} dt < ∞. The goal is to prove that under this assumption, the NSFG coherence observables ℋ(t) and Δ(t) remain bounded on [0, T^*).

steps.title: Elliptic Regularity of the Helmholtz Decomposition
steps.content: Apply the Helmholtz decomposition u = ∇ψ + ∇×A with the standard gauge ∇·A = 0. Using elliptic regularity theory, prove that the classical regularity bounds on u (specifically, the finiteness of the BKM integral and the boundedness of Sobolev norms up to order s) impose strict, non-divergent upper bounds on the Sobolev norms of ψ and A on compact subsets of the domain.
required_inputs: Classical regularity of u: u ∈ L^∞([0,T); H^s(ℝ³)) for sufficiently large s
Elliptic regularity estimates for the Poisson equation: Δψ = ∇·u, ΔA = -∇×u
required_outputs: ||ψ||_{H^{s+1}(K)} ≤ C_K (independent of t) on compact K ⊂ ℝ³
||A||_{H^{s+1}(K)} ≤ C_K (independent of t) on compact K ⊂ ℝ³
steps.epistemic_status: D_translation_hypothesis (depends on the Helmholtz decomposition being well-defined and compatible with the classical regularity bounds)
steps.promotion_condition: A proof that the Helmholtz decomposition holds with the required regularity and gauge conditions on ℝ³, and that the classical bounds on u transfer to ψ and A with constants independent of time, would promote this step to C_derived.

steps.title: Bounding the Swirl Tensor Φ
steps.content: Using the definition Φ_{μν} := ∂_μ ∂_ν ψ + (∂_μ A_ν - ∂_ν A_μ) + κ_{μν}(M), and the bounds on ψ and A from Step 2, prove that the second derivatives of Φ remain bounded in L² on the domain of interest: ||∇²Φ||_{L²} ≤ C (independent of t).
required_inputs: Bounds on ψ and A from Step 2
Vanishing of the correction term κ_{μν}(M) in the frame of analysis
steps.promotion_condition: A rigorous derivation of the bound on ||∇²Φ||_{L²} from the bounds on ψ and A, with the required regularity of the correction term κ_{μν}(M), would promote this step to C_derived.

steps.title: Bounding the Coherence Hygiene ℋ(t)
steps.content: Using the definition ℋ(t) = ∫_Ω |∇²Φ|² dx and the bound on ∇²Φ from Step 3, prove that ℋ(t) remains bounded on [0, T^*). The bound depends only on the classical regularity bounds and the domain of integration.
required_outputs: ℋ(t) ≤ C (independent of t) on [0, T^*)
steps.epistemic_status: C_derived (conditional on Steps 2 and 3 being established)

steps.title: Bounding the Coherence Phase Pressure Δ(t)
steps.content: Using the definition Δ(t) = sup_x |∂_t Φ(x,t)|, the bound on Φ from Step 3, and the classical time-regularity of u (and hence of ψ and A), prove that Δ(t) remains bounded on [0, T^*). The bound requires control of the time derivative of Φ, which in turn requires control of ∂_t ψ and ∂_t A.
required_inputs: Time regularity of u: u ∈ C^1([0,T); H^s(ℝ³)) for sufficiently large s
Bounds on ∂_t ψ and ∂_t A derived from the equations of motion
required_outputs: Δ(t) ≤ C (independent of t) on [0, T^*)
steps.promotion_condition: A rigorous derivation of the bound on Δ(t) from the classical time-regularity of u, together with the required estimates on ∂_t ψ and ∂_t A, would promote this step to C_derived.

steps.title: Conclusion by Contraposition
steps.content: From Steps 4 and 5, conclude that if classical global regularity holds (and the BKM criterion is satisfied), then ℋ(t) and Δ(t) remain strictly bounded on [0, T^*). Therefore, by contraposition, if ℋ(t) → ∞ or Δ(t) → ∞ as t → T^*, the classical solution cannot satisfy the BKM criterion, and must blow up in finite time.
required_outputs: Lemma B1: NSFG rupture ⇒ classical blow-up
steps.promotion_condition: Once Steps 2–5 are established, this conclusion follows by the contrapositive of the BKM criterion.

required_function_spaces.requirement: s sufficiently large (e.g., s > 5/2) for Sobolev embedding H^s ↪ C^1
Compact K ⊂ ℝ³; bounds uniform in t

open_obligations.obligation: Establish that the Helmholtz decomposition u = ∇ψ + ∇×A is well-defined on ℝ³ with the gauge ∇·A = 0 and with the required decay conditions for uniqueness.
Establish that the classical regularity bounds on u transfer to ψ and A with constants independent of time on compact subsets.
Provide an explicit formula for the correction term κ_{μν}(M) in the definition of Φ, or prove it vanishes in the frame of analysis.
Establish the time-regularity of ψ and A from the classical time-regularity of u, including the estimates on ∂_t ψ and ∂_t A required for bounding Δ(t).
Verify that the bounds derived in Steps 2–5 are uniform over the domain and time interval of interest, and that the constants depend only on the classical regularity bounds and the domain geometry.

content.text: The mountain does not fall because you shout; you shout because the mountain is falling.

Lemma B1 is the reverse direction of the correspondence. It does not say 'if NSFG rupture, then blow-up' as a causal claim. It says: if classical regularity holds, then NSFG coherence cannot rupture. The proof is therefore constructed by contraposition — assuming classical regularity and showing that the NSFG observables must remain bounded. The shouting is not the cause of the falling; it is a consequence of a state in which falling cannot occur.

Lemma B1 (Coercive NSFG-to-Classical Lemma) is the reverse direction of the Conditional Coherence Rupture Correspondence. It establishes that an NSFG coherence rupture — the divergence of Δ(t) or ℋ(t) — forces a classical finite-time blow-up. Because predicting classical blow-up from a structural framework requires a coercive lower estimate, the proof is constructed by contraposition of an established classical regularity criterion, specifically the Beale-Kato-Majda criterion.

content.title: Architecture for Lemma B1: Coercive NSFG-to-Classical Lemma
content.text: Objective: Prove that if classical global regularity holds (and the BKM criterion is satisfied), then the NSFG coherence observables ℋ(t) and Δ(t) remain bounded. By contraposition, if ℋ(t) → ∞ or Δ(t) → ∞, the classical solution must blow up in finite time. The proof proceeds in six steps: (1) contrapositive framing; (2) elliptic regularity of the Helmholtz decomposition; (3) bounding the swirl tensor Φ; (4) bounding the coherence hygiene ℋ(t); (5) bounding the coherence phase pressure Δ(t); (6) conclusion by contraposition.
content.latex: \text{Assume classical regularity (BKM) } \implies \mathcal{H}(t) < \infty \text{ and } \Delta(t) < \infty. \text{ Contrapositive: } \mathcal{H}(t) \to \infty \text{ or } \Delta(t) \to \infty \implies \text{classical blow-up.}
content.promotion_condition: A complete proof following the six steps with all hypotheses and function spaces made explicit, and with all open obligations discharged, would promote Lemma B1 to C_derived.

content.title: Proof Steps for Lemma B1
items: **Step 1: Contrapositive Framing.** Assume, for contradiction, that the classical velocity field u(x,t) remains globally regular on ℝ³ × [0, T^*) and satisfies the BKM criterion: ∫_0^{T^*} ||ω(t)||_{L^∞} dt < ∞. The goal is to prove that under this assumption, ℋ(t) and Δ(t) remain bounded on [0, T^*).

**Step 2: Elliptic Regularity of the Helmholtz Decomposition.** Apply u = ∇ψ + ∇×A with ∇·A = 0. Using elliptic regularity theory, prove that the classical regularity bounds on u impose strict, non-divergent upper bounds on the Sobolev norms of ψ and A on compact subsets of the domain, uniform in t.

**Step 3: Bounding the Swirl Tensor Φ.** Using Φ_{μν} := ∂_μ ∂_ν ψ + (∂_μ A_ν - ∂_ν A_μ) + κ_{μν}(M), and the bounds from Step 2, prove that ||∇²Φ||_{L²} remains bounded on the domain of interest, uniform in t.
**Step 4: Bounding the Coherence Hygiene ℋ(t).** Using ℋ(t) = ∫_Ω |∇²Φ|² dx and the bound from Step 3, prove that ℋ(t) remains bounded on [0, T^*).

**Step 5: Bounding the Coherence Phase Pressure Δ(t).** Using Δ(t) = sup_x |∂_t Φ(x,t)|, the bound from Step 3, and the classical time-regularity of u, prove that Δ(t) remains bounded on [0, T^*). This step requires control of ∂_t ψ and ∂_t A.

**Step 6: Conclusion by Contraposition.** From Steps 4 and 5, conclude that if classical global regularity holds, then ℋ(t) and Δ(t) remain bounded. Therefore, by contraposition, if ℋ(t) → ∞ or Δ(t) → ∞, the classical solution must blow up in finite time. This establishes Lemma B1.

content.title: Open Obligations for Lemma B1
content.text: The following obligations must be discharged to promote Lemma B1 from E_prediction_or_conjecture to C_derived: (i) establish that the Helmholtz decomposition is well-defined on ℝ³ with the required gauge and decay conditions; (ii) establish that classical regularity bounds on u transfer to ψ and A with constants independent of time; (iii) provide an explicit formula for the correction term κ_{μν}(M) or prove it vanishes in the frame of analysis; (iv) establish the time-regularity of ψ and A and the required estimates on ∂_t ψ and ∂_t A; (v) verify that the bounds derived in Steps 2–5 are uniform over the domain and time interval of interest.
content.latex: \text{Obligations: (i) Helmholtz well-defined; (ii) } u \text{-to-}(\psi,A) \text{ bounds; (iii) } \kappa_{\mu\nu}(M) \text{ specification; (iv) time-regularity of } \psi, A; \text{(v) uniformity of bounds.}

content.text: Lemma B1 is the most analytically demanding of the three bridge lemmas. It requires expertise in elliptic regularity theory, Sobolev embeddings, and the classical regularity theory of the Navier-Stokes equations. Unlike Lemma B2, which can draw directly on the explicit profiles of the source construction, Lemma B1 must establish a general coercive estimate that holds for any classical solution satisfying the BKM criterion. The proof architecture presented here identifies the precise steps required to discharge this obligation.

content.title: Relationship to the Conditional Coherence Rupture Correspondence
content.text: Lemma B1 is the reverse direction of the Conditional Coherence Rupture Correspondence established in Section 4.6. Together with Lemma B2 (Classical-to-NSFG Rupture) and Lemma B3 (Quotient Collapse), it would establish the full equivalence between the classical blow-up condition and the NSFG coherence rupture condition. Without Lemma B1, the reverse direction remains conjectural: the claim that NSFG rupture implies classical blow-up is an NSFG prediction, not a derived result.

content.text: The lower bound is the harder direction because it must survive the integral.

Upper bounds are permissive: a single dominant term can carry them. Lower bounds are strict: they require every cancellation to be controlled and every positive contribution to be preserved through spatial integration. Lemma B2 is a lower-bound obligation, and its architecture must therefore track every cancellation, not merely dominate the sum.

Lemma B2 is the forward direction of the conditional correspondence: it must show that the specific classical blow-up constructed in the source manuscript forces the NSFG coherence phase pressure \Delta(t) across the critical threshold \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}} at a finite positive remaining time. The obligation is not to bound \Delta(t) from above, but to establish a coercive lower bound along the active annulus and along the specific inner trajectory. This subsection expands the five-step outline from Section 9.6 into a sub-step roadmap. content.title: Lemma B2 (target statement)
content.text: For the source construction, there exist constants c_0 > 0 and \tau_0 > 0 such that \Delta_{\mathrm{OAI}}(t) \geq c_0 \tau^{-h} for all \tau \in (0, \tau_0). Here \Delta_{\mathrm{OAI}}(t) denotes the NSFG coherence phase pressure evaluated on the source construction under the Section 3 translation, and \tau = 1 - t is the remaining time before the source singular endpoint.
content.latex: \text{For the source construction, } \Delta_{\mathrm{OAI}}(t) \;\geq\; c_0 \, \tau^{-h} \;\text{ for all } \tau \in (0,\tau_0), \text{ for some } c_0 > 0, \tau_0 > 0.

content.text: The proof architecture below decomposes B2 into six sub-steps. Each sub-step names its required inputs, its target inequality, its required hypotheses, and its failure mode. The sub-steps are stated as obligations: they are what a complete proof would have to establish, not what has been established.

content.title: B2 Sub-Step Roadmap
items: **Sub-step B2.1 — Restrict to the active annulus and the inner trajectory.** Inputs: source profiles E, U, \Pi and constants X_a, X_b, h, e_0. Target: a precise statement of the domain D_{B2} = { X \in [X_a, X_b], \eta \in [-\eta_c, \eta_c], \tau \in (0, \tau_0) } together with the inner trajectory \gamma_{\mathrm{in}}(\tau) = (\sqrt{2 X_{\mathrm{in}} \tau}, 0, 0, 1-\tau). Required hypotheses: the source profiles are smooth on the closure of the annulus, the inner trajectory lies strictly inside the annulus for all \tau \in (0, \tau_0), and X_{\mathrm{in}} \in (X_a, X_b) is fixed. Failure mode: if the inner trajectory fails to lie in the annulus, the lower bound cannot be localized there and the architecture must be redirected to a different trajectory supplied by the source.

**Sub-step B2.2 — Extract the irrotational component.** Inputs: the source core velocity u^{(0)} on D_{B2}. Target: an explicit integral representation for the coherence potential \psi(x,t) = \int u^{(0)} \cdot dx restricted to the annulus, in the gauge \nabla \cdot A = 0. Required hypotheses: the Helmholtz decomposition with this gauge is unique on the source domain; the required decay or boundary conditions are satisfied on the annulus. Failure mode: if uniqueness of the Helmholtz decomposition fails on the annulus, an additional gauge-fixing argument must be supplied; the lower bound can be established under any admissible gauge provided the resulting \Phi is well-defined.

**Sub-step B2.3 — Construct \Phi on the annulus.** Inputs: the coherence potential \psi from B2.2 and the swirl torsion vector potential A. Target: the explicit tensor \Phi_{\mu
u} = \partial_\mu \partial_
u \psi + (\partial_\mu A_
u - \partial_
u A_\mu) on D_{B2}, together with its scaling with 	au. Required hypotheses: \psi and A are sufficiently smooth on the annulus for the second derivatives to exist; the correction term \kappa_{\mu
u}(M) from Section 9.2.1 vanishes on the flat-frame reference used for the comparison. Failure mode: if the correction term does not vanish in the chosen frame, an additional frame-transformation argument is required; the lower bound can be established in any frame in which the correction is controlled.

**Sub-step B2.4 — Compute \partial_t \Phi and isolate its non-cancelling part.** Inputs: the tensor \Phi from B2.3 and the source time-scaling \tau = 1 - t. Target: an explicit expression for \partial_t \Phi on D_{B2} in terms of the source profiles, with the leading contribution identified and separated from sub-leading terms. Required hypotheses: the source profiles are differentiable in t on the annulus; the leading contribution does not cancel identically. Failure mode: if the leading contribution cancels along \gamma_{\mathrm{in}}, a different trajectory or a different component of \Phi must be selected; the cancellation must be shown to be non-generic before redirecting.

**Sub-step B2.5 — Establish the pointwise lower bound along \gamma_{\mathrm{in}}.** Inputs: the leading contribution from B2.4, the source amplitude e_0, and the source exponent h. Target: a pointwise inequality |\partial_t \Phi(\gamma_{\mathrm{in}}(\tau))| \geq c_1 \tau^{-1-h} for all \tau \in (0, \tau_0), for some c_1 > 0. Required hypotheses: the leading contribution is strictly positive along \gamma_{\mathrm{in}}; sub-leading terms are bounded above by a small multiple of the leading term; the constant c_1 is uniform in \tau and determined by e_0 and the annulus geometry. Failure mode: if the leading contribution is not strictly positive, a sign-definite lower bound on a suitable norm must be established; a bound on |\partial_t \Phi| alone does not yield the coercive conclusion.

**Sub-step B2.6 — Convert the pointwise bound to the phase pressure bound and cross the threshold.** Inputs: the pointwise bound from B2.5 and the NSFG definition \Delta(t) = \sup_x |\partial_t \Phi(x,t)|. Target: the inequality \Delta_{\mathrm{OAI}}(t) \geq c_0 \tau^{-h} for all \tau \in (0, \tau_0), together with the threshold-crossing statement \Delta_{\mathrm{OAI}}(t_{\mathrm{crit}}) = \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}} at a finite positive \tau_{\mathrm{crit}} = (c_0 / \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}})^{1/h}. Required hypotheses: the supremum in the definition of \Delta is attained or approached along \gamma_{\mathrm{in}} for \tau sufficiently small; \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}} is finite and positive. Failure mode: if the supremum is not approached along \gamma_{\mathrm{in}}, the lower bound must be established on a suitable neighborhood of \gamma_{\mathrm{in}} within the annulus.

content.title: Intermediate inequalities required for B2
content.text: The following intermediate inequalities are the target obligations of sub-steps B2.4 through B2.6. They are stated as one-sided lower bounds; none of them may be reversed to obtain an upper bound.
content.interpretation: Inequality (B2-i) is the pointwise lower bound along the inner trajectory. Inequality (B2-ii) lifts it to the phase pressure by the definition of \Delta as a spatial supremum. Equation (B2-iii) is the threshold-crossing statement, which is an arithmetic consequence of (B2-ii) given finite positive \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}. None of these inequalities may be used in the reverse direction.

content.title: Explicit constants required for B2
content.text: The proof of B2 must supply explicit expressions, or at least explicit bounds, for the constants c_1 and c_0 in the intermediate inequalities. These constants must depend only on the source profiles, the annulus geometry, and the exponent h; they must not depend on \tau.
content.latex: c_1 = c_1(E, U, \Pi, X_a, X_b, \eta_c, h, e_0), \quad c_0 = c_0(c_1, \text{annulus geometry}).
content.interpretation: The constants must be uniform in \tau for the lower bound to be coercive. A \tau-dependent constant would not yield the threshold crossing at a finite positive \tau_{\mathrm{crit}}.

content.title: Failure Modes and Redirects for B2
items: **Cancellation along \gamma_{\mathrm{in}}.** If the leading contribution to \partial_t \Phi cancels identically along the inner trajectory, the proof must either (a) select a different trajectory inside the annulus on which the leading contribution is strictly sign-definite, or (b) establish a sign-definite lower bound on a norm of \partial_t \Phi rather than on its pointwise value. In case (b), the resulting bound on \Delta must still be coercive.

**Non-uniqueness of the Helmholtz decomposition.** If the gauge \nabla\cdot A = 0 fails to yield a unique (\psi, A) pair on the annulus, an additional gauge-fixing condition must be supplied. The lower bound may be established in any admissible gauge provided the resulting \Phi is well-defined and the pointwise bound survives the gauge change.

**Frame-dependent correction term.** If the correction \kappa_{\mu\nu}(M) in the definition of \Phi does not vanish in the frame used for the comparison, a frame-transformation argument is required to control its contribution to \partial_t \Phi. The correction must be bounded by a small multiple of the leading contribution for the lower bound to survive.

**Loss of uniformity in \tau.** If the constants c_1 or c_0 depend on \tau, the lower bound is not coercive. The proof must either exhibit \tau-independent constants or establish the bound on a shrinking family of annuli whose geometry compensates the \tau-dependence. In the latter case, the threshold-crossing statement must be re-derived from the compensated bound.

**Threshold crossing beyond the source endpoint.** If the lower bound only establishes \Delta_{\mathrm{OAI}}(t) \geq c_0 \tau^{-h} for \tau in a range that does not include \tau_{\mathrm{crit}}, the threshold-crossing statement cannot be concluded. The proof must extend the lower bound to all \tau \in (0, \tau_0) with \tau_0 > \tau_{\mathrm{crit}}.

content.text: The six sub-steps above decompose B2 into three logically distinct obligations: the localization obligation (B2.1), the construction obligation (B2.2 through B2.4), and the coercivity obligation (B2.5 and B2.6). The localization obligation is finite-dimensional and depends only on the source profiles and the annulus geometry. The construction obligation depends on the Helmholtz decomposition and the definition of \Phi; it is a translation hypothesis at the level of the NSFG mapping. The coercivity obligation is the load-bearing step: it is where the lower bound must survive the definition of \Delta as a spatial supremum and where the threshold crossing must be established at a finite positive \tau.

content.title: Promotion conditions for the sub-steps of B2
content.text: Each sub-step of B2 carries its own promotion condition. Discharging all six sub-steps, together with the explicit constants, promotes Lemma B2 from E_prediction_or_conjecture to C_derived. The promotion conditions are cumulative: the failure of any sub-step blocks the promotion of the lemma as a whole.
content.latex: \text{Promotion of B2} \iff \text{B2.1} \wedge \text{B2.2} \wedge \text{B2.3} \wedge \text{B2.4} \wedge \text{B2.5} \wedge \text{B2.6} \text{ all discharged with explicit constants.}
content.interpretation: The conjunction is strict. A proof that discharges B2.1 through B2.5 but fails B2.6 does not promote the lemma; it establishes a weaker statement that does not by itself yield the threshold crossing. Similarly, a proof that discharges B2.5 with \tau-dependent constants does not satisfy B2.6's uniformity requirement.

content.text: The B2 architecture is deliberately stated as a roadmap rather than a proof. Every sub-step is an obligation; every inequality is a target; every constant is an explicit unknown. The discipline of the epistemic status taxonomy requires that the lemma remain labeled E_prediction_or_conjecture until the conjunction of sub-steps is discharged. This preserves the distinction between the source-supported classical content of the OpenAI construction and the proposed NSFG interpretation of that content, and it keeps the load-bearing bridge from being mistaken for a completed crossing.

content.title: Relationship of B2 to B1 and B3
content.text: Lemma B2 is the forward direction of the conditional correspondence: it takes the source blow-up as its input and produces an NSFG rupture as its output. Lemma B1 is the reverse direction: it takes an NSFG rupture as its input and produces a classical blow-up as its output. Lemma B3 is the NSFG-internal step that connects an NSFG rupture to a collapse of the observer-relative coherence quotient. B2 is the most immediately tractable of the three because the source supplies explicit profiles that can be integrated directly; B1 requires a coercive lower estimate; B3 requires an argument within the NSFG axiomatic floor.
content.latex: \text{B2: classical} \to \text{NSFG rupture}; \quad \text{B1: NSFG rupture} \to \text{classical}; \quad \text{B3: NSFG rupture} \to \text{quotient collapse}.
content.epistemic_status: E_prediction_or_conjecture for each of B1, B2, B3

Discharging B2 alone establishes the forward direction of the correspondence but not the reverse direction or the quotient collapse. subsections.subtitle: From Supercritical Motif Tension to Zero-Dimensional Accessible Quotient
subsections.purpose: To provide a structured proof architecture for Lemma B3 of Section 4.6, which asserts that an NSFG coherence rupture (Δ(t) reaching or exceeding Δ_crit) necessitates the collapse of the observer-relative accessible coherence quotient ℳ_C^O(h,x) to a Convergence Boundary. This subsection specifies the required steps, the NSFG axioms each step depends on, the obligations that remain unproved, and the falsification conditions under which the architecture would need revision. It does not claim that any step has been completed.
