math.label: Lemma B3 (statement to be proved)

variables.meaning: Continuous observer-relative accessible distinguishability functional (NSFG definition, §9.2.6)

assumptions: Δ(t) and Δ_crit are NSFG-internal definitions; they do not depend on the source construction.
The implication is to be proved within the NSFG axiomatic floor: XOR, Library, observer-relative coherence, and the coherence quotient framework.
The structural statement dim(ℳ_C^O(h,x)) = 0 is discrete; the continuous statement D_O → 0 is carried by the continuous functional D_O, not by the dimension.
The statement does not assert anything about the classical Navier-Stokes solution; that link is provided by B1 and B2.

math.label: Step B3.1 — Triadic closure failure under supercritical tension
math.obligation: Prove that when motif tension reaches the critical threshold, the Gate-16 triadic closure condition Θ_n = 0 fails at a rate that does not decay as Δ grows. This requires specifying the functional relationship between Δ(t) and the closure error rate Θ_n(t).

variables.meaning: Triadic closure error (Gate-16 stability indicator; see PHYS-CORE-013 Appendix D)

dependencies: PHYS-CORE-013 Appendix D (Gate-16 and Triadic Stability Structures)
PHYS-CORE-007 Section 8.1 (Braid Collapse and Field Decoherence)
assumptions: The relationship between Δ and Θ_n is not yet specified; specifying it is part of the obligation.
The proof must not assume that Θ_n is itself monotone in Δ; it must establish that closure fails on a set of paths of non-vanishing measure.
math.falsification_condition: A demonstration that Θ_n = 0 is preserved for all admissible paths even when Δ ≥ Δ_crit would falsify B3.1 and force revision of Lemma B3.

math.label: Step B3.2 — Phase permutation injection rate
math.obligation: Establish a lower bound on the rate at which triadic closure failure injects unstructured phase permutations into the motif braid, and show that this rate exceeds the observer's integration rate 1/τ_obs once Δ ≥ Δ_crit. This step converts the qualitative failure of B3.1 into a quantitative bound.

variables.meaning: Observer integration time (a parameter of O; not fixed by the axiomatic floor)

dependencies: PHYS-CORE-000 (Primer) for the definition of observer-relative resolution
assumptions: τ_obs is observer-relative and not fixed by the axiomatic floor; its value is part of the observer specification.
The bound must be lower, not upper; an upper bound on the injection rate would be insufficient (see §9.2.4).
The rate comparison must hold on the same time scale on which the observer evaluates coherence.
math.falsification_condition: A demonstration that the phase permutation injection rate remains bounded strictly below I_N(O)/τ_obs even when Δ ≥ Δ_crit would falsify B3.2.

math.label: Step B3.3 — Distinction metric upper bound
math.obligation: Derive an explicit upper bound on the observer-relative distinction magnitude δ_O between any two coherent continuation paths, expressed in terms of I_N(O) and a function g(Δ(t)) that tends to or below 1 when Δ ≥ Δ_crit. This is the central analytic step of B3.

variables.meaning: Observer-relative distinction magnitude between two coherent paths
A function satisfying g(\Delta) \leq 1 for \Delta \geq \Delta_{\mathrm{crit}}; its form is an obligation of this step

assumptions: δ_O is defined via the observer's effective distinction function; the explicit formula is an obligation of this step (compare §9.2.6 for D_O).
The bound must be uniform over all path pairs γ_1, γ_2 in Γ_O(h,x); a bound holding only for specific pairs would be insufficient.
The proof must not assume that Γ_O(h,x) is finite.
math.falsification_condition: Exhibition of a path pair γ_1, γ_2 in Γ_O(h,x) for which δ_O(γ_1, γ_2) > I_N(O) for all t despite Δ ≥ Δ_crit would falsify B3.3 and hence B3.

math.label: Step B3.4 — Path indistinguishability
math.obligation: Combine the bound of Step B3.3 with the observer-relative coherence equivalence definition (PHYS-CORE-013 Definition 3.2) to conclude that all coherent continuation paths become observer-relative equivalent once Δ ≥ Δ_crit. This step is largely definitional, but requires care: the equivalence relation ∼_O must be shown to be applicable to the limiting behavior of the paths.
assumptions: The observer-relative coherence relation is applied at each time t along the path; the collapse is not instantaneous but monotone.
The equivalence relation is assumed to be well-defined on the relevant class of paths; this is part of the NSFG axiomatic floor.
math.falsification_condition: A demonstration that γ_1 and γ_2 can remain distinguishable under ∼_O even when δ_O < I_N(O) would falsify the definitional step and require revision of the definition of ∼_O.

math.label: Step B3.5 — Discrete quotient collapse
math.obligation: Show that when all coherent paths in Γ_O(h,x) are observer-relative equivalent, the accessible quotient ℳ_C^O(h,x) contains a single equivalence class, and hence its structural dimension is 0. This step converts path-level indistinguishability into quotient-level collapse.

variables.meaning: Discrete/topological dimension of the accessible quotient

assumptions: The quotient dimension is discrete/topological; it is not assigned a continuous power law.
The proof must address the case where Γ_O(h,x) is infinite but collapses to a single equivalence class.
math.falsification_condition: A demonstration that the quotient can retain positive structural dimension while all paths in Γ_O(h,x) are ∼_O-equivalent would falsify B3.5.

math.label: Step B3.6 — Continuous collapse of D_O
math.obligation: Establish that the continuous accessibility functional D_O tends to zero along the rupture path, and that the limit is consistent with the discrete collapse of Step B3.5 (D_O = 0 ⇔ dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0). This step bridges the discrete structural collapse and the continuous observable collapse.
assumptions: D_O is defined by its properties in §9.2.6; an explicit formula is an open obligation and may be supplied either as part of B3.6 or separately.
The limit D_O → 0 is to be understood along the specific rupture path; the statement is path-dependent and not uniform in (h,x).
math.falsification_condition: A demonstration that D_O remains bounded below by a positive constant along a path with Δ ≥ Δ_crit for all t would falsify B3.6 and, together with B3.5, force revision of the link between the discrete and continuous descriptions.

math.label: Step B3.7 — Non-triviality of the collapse (exclusion of trivial cases)
math.obligation: Prove that the collapse of ℳ_C^O(h,x) is not vacuous: that Γ_O(h,x) is non-empty at the rupture time, so that the statement 'all paths are equivalent' is not trivially true because there are no paths. This step guards against a degenerate proof of B3.
assumptions: The nonempty continuation requirement is part of the NSFG axiomatic framework (PHYS-CORE-000); the obligation is to verify it at the rupture point.
The proof must address the possibility that the rupture drives Γ_O(h,x) to empty, which would require a separate treatment (cf. Pathway to Nowhere, PHYS-CORE-013 Section 4.5).
math.falsification_condition: A demonstration that Γ_O(h,x) is empty at the rupture point would not falsify B3 but would require distinguishing the case from the Convergence Boundary collapse; it would suggest a Pathway to Nowhere rather than a Convergence Boundary.

math.label: Step B3.8 — Synthesis of Lemma B3
math.obligation: Combine Steps B3.1 through B3.7 into the statement of Lemma B3. This step is purely logical assembly: it requires that each prior step be discharged with the stated obligations satisfied, and that no additional assumptions be introduced. The synthesis must preserve the epistemic status of each component.
assumptions: No step of B3 depends on the specific source construction or on the classical Navier-Stokes variables; the proof is internal to NSFG.
The synthesis does not claim that the preceding steps have been completed; it specifies the assembly that would promote B3 to C_derived.
math.falsification_condition: Failure of any of Steps B3.1--B3.7 would falsify the synthesis as a whole. Partial success (some steps discharged, others not) leaves B3 in the status E_prediction_or_conjecture.

content.text: the traveler does not lose the road; the traveler loses the ability to tell one road from another

Lemma B3 is not about paths ceasing to exist. It is about the observer ceasing to be able to distinguish one path from another. The collapse is a collapse of distinguishability, not of the Library. The traveler keeps walking; the roads converge beneath their feet.

Lemma B3 is the load-bearing structural lemma of the conditional correspondence. It bridges the NSFG-internal rupture criterion (Δ(t) reaching Δ_crit) to the NSFG-internal structural statement (collapse of the observer-relative accessible quotient). Unlike B1 and B2, which connect NSFG to classical Navier-Stokes variables, B3 is entirely internal to NSFG: its proof must be carried out within the axiomatic floor established in PHYS-CORE-000 and refined in PHYS-CORE-013. This subsection provides a step-by-step proof architecture for B3. It does not claim that any step has been completed.

content.title: Lemma B3 (statement to be proved)
content.text: Let Δ(t) be the NSFG coherence phase pressure and Δ_crit the critical coherence threshold. Then, within the NSFG axiomatic framework, Δ(t) ≥ Δ_crit implies that the observer-relative accessible coherence quotient ℳ_C^O(h,x) collapses to zero dimension and the continuous accessibility functional D_O(h,x,t) tends to zero along the rupture path.
content.interpretation: The statement is a target, not a theorem. Its proof requires the eight steps below, each of which is itself an obligation.

content.title: Proof Steps for Lemma B3
items: **Step B3.1 — Triadic closure failure.** Show that Δ(t) ≥ Δ_crit forces the Gate-16 triadic closure condition Θ_n = 0 to fail with non-vanishing intensity. The relationship between Δ and Θ_n is an obligation of this step; it must not be assumed without derivation. (Depends on PHYS-CORE-013 Appendix D.)

**Step B3.2 — Phase permutation injection rate.** Establish a lower bound on the rate at which triadic closure failure injects unstructured phase permutations into the motif braid, and show that this rate exceeds the observer integration rate I_N(O)/τ_obs once Δ ≥ Δ_crit. The bound must be lower, not upper; an upper bound would be insufficient (cf. §9.2.4). (Depends on B3.1 and PHYS-CORE-013 §3.2.)

**Step B3.3 — Distinction metric upper bound.** Derive an explicit upper bound on the observer-relative distinction magnitude δ_O between any two coherent continuation paths, expressed in terms of I_N(O) and a function g(Δ) that is at most 1 when Δ ≥ Δ_crit. This is the central analytic step of B3. The explicit formula for δ_O is an obligation. (Depends on B3.2 and PHYS-CORE-013 Definition 3.2.)

**Step B3.4 — Path indistinguishability.** Combine B3.3 with the definition of ∼_O to conclude that all coherent paths in Γ_O(h,x) are observer-relative equivalent once Δ ≥ Δ_crit. (Depends on B3.3 and PHYS-CORE-013 Definition 3.2.)

**Step B3.5 — Discrete quotient collapse.** Show that when all coherent paths are ∼_O-equivalent, the accessible quotient contains a single equivalence class and its structural dimension is 0. (Depends on B3.4 and PHYS-CORE-013 Definition 3.3.)

**Step B3.6 — Continuous collapse of D_O.** Establish that the continuous accessibility functional D_O tends to zero along the rupture path, consistent with the discrete collapse of B3.5. The explicit formula for D_O is an obligation of this step or of §9.2.6. (Depends on B3.5 and §9.2.6.)

**Step B3.7 — Non-triviality of the collapse.** Prove that the collapse is not vacuous: Γ_O(h,x) is non-empty at the rupture time, so the statement 'all paths are equivalent' is not trivially true. (Depends on PHYS-CORE-000 and PHYS-CORE-013 §2.)

**Step B3.8 — Synthesis.** Assemble B3.1–B3.7 into the statement of Lemma B3. No additional assumptions may be introduced at synthesis; each component step must be discharged with its stated obligations satisfied.

content.text: Several caveats distinguish this architecture from a completed proof. First, the relationship between Δ(t) and the triadic closure error Θ_n is not yet specified; B3.1 must derive it, not assume it. Second, the lower bound on the phase permutation injection rate in B3.2 must be uniform over the path family Γ_O(h,x); a bound holding only for specific paths would be insufficient. Third, the explicit formula for the distinction metric δ_O in B3.3 is an open specification task, analogous to the open specification of D_O in §9.2.6. Fourth, B3.5 must address the case where Γ_O(h,x) is infinite but collapses to a single equivalence class; the quotient dimension is discrete, and the proof must not assign it a continuous power law. Fifth, B3.7 must distinguish the case of a non-empty collapse (Convergence Boundary) from the case of an empty continuation set (Pathway to Nowhere, PHYS-CORE-013 §4.5).

content.title: Falsification Conditions for Lemma B3
content.text: Lemma B3 would be falsified by any of the following: (i) a demonstration that Θ_n = 0 is preserved for all admissible paths even when Δ ≥ Δ_crit; (ii) a demonstration that the phase permutation injection rate remains strictly below I_N(O)/τ_obs when Δ ≥ Δ_crit; (iii) an exhibition of a path pair with δ_O(γ_1, γ_2) > I_N(O) for all t despite Δ ≥ Δ_crit; (iv) a demonstration that the quotient retains positive structural dimension while all paths in Γ_O(h,x) are ∼_O-equivalent; (v) a demonstration that D_O remains bounded below by a positive constant along a path with Δ ≥ Δ_crit for all t; (vi) a demonstration that Γ_O(h,x) is empty at the rupture point, which would suggest a Pathway to Nowhere rather than a Convergence Boundary and would require a separate treatment.
content.latex: \text{B3 is falsified by any of (i)--(vi) above.}
content.interpretation: The falsification conditions are stated explicitly so that the target is testable within the NSFG axiomatic framework. A partial success would leave B3 in status E; only full discharge of B3.1--B3.8 would promote B3 to C_derived.

content.title: Promotion Conditions for Lemma B3
content.text: Promotion of B3 from E_prediction_or_conjecture to C_derived requires: (a) specification of the functional relationship between Δ(t) and Θ_n(t); (b) derivation of the lower bound on the phase permutation injection rate; (c) specification of the explicit formula for the distinction metric δ_O; (d) proof that the quotient dimension is 0 when all coherent paths are ∼_O-equivalent; (e) specification of the explicit formula for D_O and proof of the consistency condition D_O = 0 ⇔ dim(ℳ_C^O) = 0; (f) proof of non-triviality of the collapse; (g) assembly of B3.1--B3.7 without additional assumptions.
content.latex: \text{Promotion of B3 requires discharge of (a)--(g) above.}
content.interpretation: The promotion conditions name the exact mathematical labor required to convert B3 from a roadmap into a derived lemma. They do not claim that any part of this labor has been completed.

content.text: The B3 architecture is the structural complement of B1 and B2. B1 and B2 connect NSFG to classical Navier-Stokes variables; B3 connects the NSFG rupture criterion to the NSFG structural collapse. Together, the three lemmas would establish the conditional correspondence of Section 4.6. Discharging B3 alone would not establish the correspondence; it would establish the structural half of it. Discharging all three would promote the conditional correspondence from the status D_translation_hypothesis (forward) and E_prediction_or_conjecture (reverse) to a proved theorem, conditional only on the hypotheses of the source construction.
